## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sujātājātaka* (Ja 306), translated in English as *Queen Sujātā*, is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana, its contextual frame narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) concerns a domestic rift between King Pasenadi of Kosala and Queen Mallikā [SuttaCentral; Galasek 2016]. Following what the commentary terms a "bedroom quarrel" (*sayanakalaho*) or harem dispute regarding conjugal relations, the king refused to speak to Mallikā and treated her as though she did not exist, claiming that luxury and status had gone to her head [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Galasek 2016]. When visiting the palace, the Buddha noted her absence, reminded the king that he himself had elevated Mallikā to her royal status, and praised the blessings of amity, successfully reconciling the royal couple [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Galasek 2016]. To illustrate the folly of their friction, the Buddha related an incident from their past lives, introduced with the opening inquiry, "What is this egg-shaped fruit" [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral do not list any cross-language versions in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit collections [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus likewise records no cross-language matches above threshold, but identifies five internal text-reuse alignments with the third volume of the Pali *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, centered on the verses shared across segments 1.4–3.4 [DharmaNexus].
